input.prompt:
Step 11 of the approved design doc at `.claude/plans/clubspot-directus-sync.md`. Deploy `packages/clubspot-sync` as a scheduled Cloud Run job.

**Read the doc's "Authentication to Directus" and "GCP identity" sections first.** The auth section was rewritten two commits ago specifically for the post-#124 structure — the older description in this repo's history is wrong and cites files that no longer exist.

## Structure you are working in

There are now four Pulumi projects under `packages/infrastructure/src/`: `bootstrap/`, `infrastructure/`, `crm/`, and the shared non-project `directus/`. `just deploy` applies infrastructure then crm. #124 established the split; this session renamed its `people-hub` project to `crm`.

## Task

**1. The service account**, in `src/bootstrap/`. `src/bootstrap/report-runner.ts` is the model — read it. Identities live in the bootstrap stack, which is applied separately by `just deploy-bootstrap`. Use `ServiceAccount` from `../service-account` and its `allowImpersonation`.

Use `humanDeployer` from `src/config.ts` rather than hardcoding an address — `report-runner.ts:10` hardcodes a list, and the design doc explicitly says not to copy that.

Export it the way the others are, and make sure `src/infrastructure/identities.ts` can read it — that file is how the infrastructure project consumes bootstrap's identities across the stack boundary.

**2. The Directus token secret.** `randomSecret("clubspot-sync-directus-token")` in `src/infrastructure/directus.ts`, alongside `directusKey` / `directusSecret` / `directusDbPassword` (`:32-38`). Pulumi generates and owns the value; nothing is set out of band.

**3. `DirectusUser` gains an optional `token` input.** It currently takes `email`, `roleId`, `provider`, `externalIdentifier` (`src/directus/resources.ts:328-342`) and provisions OIDC users only. Add `token?: pulumi.Input<string>` and pass it through on **both** create and update. The machine user uses `provider: "default"` with no external identifier.

This is a change to a shared resource used by the existing `crm-staff-ungood` user — make it strictly additive so that user's behavior is unchanged when `token` is absent.

**4. The sync role and machine user**, in `src/infrastructure/directus-roles.ts`, beside Staff/Coach/Guardian. A `DirectusRole` named "Clubspot Sync", `appAccess: false`. Then export its policy id as a stack output from `src/infrastructure/index.ts` (`:25-27` shows the pattern), and read it in `src/crm/refs.ts` (`stringOutput`).

**5. The permission rules**, in `src/crm/index.ts` as `DirectusPermissionRule` resources — *not* on the role. They name collections, so they need the schema applied first; the role does not. That is #124's own rationale, stated in `directus-roles.ts:9-13`.

The doc's permission table is the spec. **The one that is easy to get wrong: `session_classes` needs `delete`**, unlike every other collection. The sync cancels rather than deletes everywhere else, but `session_classes` is a pure join with no status field, so a class a session no longer offers is removed outright (`DirectusClient.deleteItem`). A role without that permission passes review and then 403s the first time a session drops a class. Everything else is create/read/update only.

**6. The image and job.** A `clubspot-sync` target in the root `Dockerfile` — the existing `report-runner` target (`:13-17`) shows the `pnpm deploy --filter` pattern. Then a `gcp.cloudrunv2.Job` plus a `gcp.cloudscheduler.Job` in a new file under `src/infrastructure/`, modelled on `run-reports-job.ts`.

Environment for the job: `CLUBSPOT_CLUB_ID`, `DIRECTUS_URL`, and secrets `CLUBSPOT_EMAIL` / `CLUBSPOT_PASSWORD` / `DIRECTUS_TOKEN` via `secretKeyRef` (`run-reports-job.ts:82-98` is the shape). The Clubspot secrets already exist as `clubspot-username` / `clubspot-password`; grant the new service account access with `secret.grant(...)` rather than creating new secrets.

Set `buildOnPreview: false` on the image, as `run-reports-job.ts:42-43` now does — #114 is about exactly this, and a preview that rebuilds an image is the thing that issue exists to stop.

Pick a schedule that makes sense for a sync with a 24-hour refresh floor and say why in a comment. `run-reports-job.ts` runs hourly 9am–9pm PST; you do not have to match it.

## Scope fence

- Do NOT modify anything under `packages/clubspot-sync/src` or `test`. The application is done; this step deploys it.
- Do NOT modify `packages/crm/schema.yaml` or `docs/crm-schema.md`.
- Do NOT change the existing Staff/Coach/Guardian roles, their rules, `crm-staff-ungood`, or `run-reports-job.ts` beyond what is needed to read a shared value.
- Do NOT run `pulumi up`, `just deploy`, or `just deploy-bootstrap`. The human applies. `just preview` will not work either — the `crm` stack has not been initialized yet.
- Do NOT update `CLAUDE.md`'s package list — step 13.

## Acceptance

- `just ci` passes. That is the only automated gate available, since nothing can be applied from here.
- `tsc` accepts all four Pulumi projects.
- The `session_classes` delete permission is present.
- `DirectusUser` without a `token` behaves exactly as before.

Report the schedule you chose and anything the brief did not anticipate.

Commit once.

**Noticed, left alone (pre-existing, out of scope):** the Dockerfile's `COPY packages/people-hub/package.json packages/people-hub/` line (for pnpm's lockfile-completeness workaround, #114) still references the old `people-hub` package name/path, which no longer exists post-rename. **Step 11 landed** (`f56950e2`), and reviewing it caught a bug from *my own* rename work (`8ab25bdf`).

**`Dockerfile:27` still copied `packages/people-hub/package.json`** — a path the rename deleted. Any image build would have failed on a missing file. My rename grep used `--include` extension filters, and `Dockerfile` has no extension, so both the original rename and the follow-up missed it. A `git grep` with no filters found it plus one stale prose line in `Caddyfile`. Both fixed.

The sub-agent caught something good on its own, too: **adding a second `FROM ... AS` stage changes Docker's default build target** to the last stage. `run-reports-job.ts`'s image never set `target`, so it would have silently started building `clubspot-sync` instead. It pinned `target: "report-runner"`. I verified both images now pin their targets explicitly.

I also set `infrastructure:clubspotClubId: nw6IMf9Bnq` in `Pulumi.prod.yaml`. The new job declares it as *required* config, so leaving it unset fails the apply. That's the club id I verified live against Clubspot earlier — it appears in dashboard URLs and isn't a secret, so it belongs in per-stack config beside the domains rather than as a manual step you'd hit mid-deploy.

Schedule chosen: every six hours, comfortably inside the 24-hour refresh floor.

`just ci` green — 188 tests.

**Step 13 is running** (README + CLAUDE.md). I told it to fix the *whole* package list, not just its own addition — CLAUDE.md claims 7 packages and omits `crm`, `portal`, and `substrate`, all of which predate this session. # Review the Diff

Dispatch a sub-agent to review everything on the session branch. It reports findings. It does not fix them without being asked.

## 1. Collect the diff

```sh
git fetch origin main
git diff origin/main...HEAD --stat
git log origin/main..HEAD --oneline
```

If the diff is empty, say so and stop.

## 2. Dispatch the reviewer

Use `Agent` with `subagent_type: reviewer`.

The checklist lives in `.claude/agents/reviewer.md` — correctness, secrets and auth, infrastructure, TypeScript, prose, and scope. Do not repeat it in the prompt. Tell the agent only:

- The branch point to diff against, normally `origin/main...HEAD`.
- Anything in the batch that deserves extra attention, such as a change to auth or IAM.
- Anything already known and deliberate, so it does not report it as a finding.

The agent is read-only by construction. It has no `Edit` or `Write` tool, so it cannot fix what it finds.

## 3. Skip it when it cannot help

A review costs time. Skip it and say why when the whole diff is prose — markdown, comments, docs — because every item on the checklist is about code. Read the diff yourself instead.

Never skip a review when the diff touches auth, IAM, secrets, or `packages/infrastructure`.

## 4. Report

Give the user the findings grouped by severity. For each one, say whether you recommend fixing it now or capturing it as an issue.

Ask before fixing anything. The user decides. To fix, dispatch through `implement` so the fix gets its own commit.

input.prompt:
Review the full session diff on `session/clubspot-directus` against `origin/main...HEAD`. 21 commits, 64 files, ~8200 insertions. Issues #69 and #70: Clubspot data now syncs into the CRM's Directus instance instead of Google Sheets, and the job's configuration is camp discovery plus a sync log rather than a config spreadsheet.

The approved design doc is `.claude/plans/clubspot-directus-sync.md`. Read it — several choices in this diff are deliberate and only make sense against it.

## Deserves extra attention

- **`packages/infrastructure`** — a new `clubspot-sync` service account in the bootstrap stack, a generated Directus static token in Secret Manager, a new `token` input on the shared `DirectusUser` dynamic resource, a new Directus role plus its policy-keyed permission rules split across two Pulumi projects, and a new Cloud Run job with a Scheduler trigger. IAM and least privilege matter here.
- **The Directus permission rules** in `packages/infrastructure/src/crm/index.ts`. `session_classes` is deliberately the only collection granted `delete`; everything else is create/read/update. If the sync writes a collection the rules don't cover, it 403s in production and nothing here would catch it — cross-check the rule list against what the code actually writes.
- **Person identity** (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/people.ts`, `person-sync.ts`). A person reference is resolved once at row creation and never re-resolved; that is what makes a manual merge durable. Any path that recomputes `person_id` for an existing row is a serious bug.
- **The merge of #124** (`4bddcdbf`) and the rename that follows it (`65e794fb`). #124 restructured `packages/infrastructure` while this session had renamed `people-hub` to `crm`. Check nothing was lost or half-renamed — particularly that no path still resolves to a `people-hub` location.
- **Secrets.** `CLUBSPOT_EMAIL` / `CLUBSPOT_PASSWORD` / `DIRECTUS_TOKEN` reach the job through `secretKeyRef`. Check nothing logs a token or accepts one in a way that puts it in `ps` (#49 is about exactly that).

## Known and deliberate — do not report these

- **`packages/crm/schema.yaml` is generated**, not hand-written, by `directus schema snapshot` against a real instance. Its size and formatting are not review material. The same goes for `pnpm-lock.yaml`.
- **The Directus roles are recreated rather than aliased.** The user explicitly accepted this: the CRM holds no data and the `crm` Pulumi stack has never been initialized.
- **`packages/clubspot-sync` duplicates ~40 lines of `fetch` plumbing** from `packages/infrastructure/src/directus/client.ts`. An app package must not depend on the deployment package; extracting a shared client is deferred in the design doc.
- **The sync sends no Google Chat notifications.** Deferred to #122, along with where `notifications.ts` should live.
- **Two of the five old reports are not replaced.** `sessions`' capacity aggregate is #123; the rest stay until a human disables their rows in the Reports worksheet.
- **`refs.ts:4` still names `.claude/plans/people-hub-project-split.md`.** That is #124's historical design record and keeps its filename.
- **Pre-existing `no-explicit-any` warnings** in `clubspot-sdk/src/parse.ts` and `gsuite/src/calendar.ts`.
- **Step 12 of the plan (deploy and verify) has not run.** Nothing here has been applied; `just preview` cannot run because the `crm` stack is not initialized yet.

## Worth knowing

`just ci` passes: 16 test files, 188 tests, 0 errors. The plan functions are pure and directly unit-tested; the Parse and Directus boundaries are thin executors, stubbed in tests.

Report findings grouped by severity. Be specific with `path:line`. If you believe something is a bug, say what input produces the wrong behavior.

**All twelve implementable steps are done.** Step 13 landed (`d32748dd`), plus one inline fix (`c5520091`).

CLAUDE.md's package list went from 7 to 11 — `crm`, `portal`, and `substrate` were missing before this session even started. Its Testing section no longer claims coverage is "thin: only `packages/gsuite/test/spreadsheet.test.ts` exists"; there are 188 tests across 16 files. The Deployment section now describes three Pulumi projects instead of one. I added `just directus-local` to Common Commands myself, since it's this session's entry point for local work, and corrected `just ci`'s description — it runs install and test too.

**Review is running** on the full 21-commit diff. I flagged the areas that actually carry risk — the IAM and Secret Manager additions, the permission rules (if the sync writes a collection the rules don't cover, it 403s in production and nothing in CI would catch it), the never-re-resolve invariant on person identity, and whether the #124 merge left anything half-renamed. I also listed the deliberate choices so it doesn't report them as findings.

**What's left is yours — step 12:**

```
pulumi stack init prod --cwd ./packages/infrastructure/src/crm   # one time only
just refresh
just deploy                                                       # infrastructure, then crm
```

Then the verification the plan calls for: a `--dry-run` first, then one finished camp with `--camp <id>`, checked in the Directus UI before the scheduler takes over.

I'll bring you the review findings, then open the PR.

input.command:
gh pr create --base main --head session/clubspot-directus --title "Sync Clubspot into the CRM instead of spreadsheets" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Issues #69 and #70. Clubspot data now syncs into the CRM's Directus instance instead of Google
Sheets tabs, and the job's configuration is camp discovery plus a sync log rather than the "Reports"
config worksheet.

Design doc: `.claude/plans/clubspot-directus-sync.md`.

## What's here

- **`people-hub` renamed to `crm`** — the package, the doc, the Pulumi project, and the resource
  names. Roles are recreated rather than aliased: the CRM holds no data and its stack has never been
  initialized, so there was nothing to protect.
- **`packages/clubspot-sync`** — a new package that reads Clubspot and writes the CRM through
  Directus's REST API. Pure plan functions plus thin executors, so the mapping is unit-testable with
  no Directus and no Parse.
- **Schema changes** — `registration_billing`, `custom_field_definitions`, `custom_field_responses`,
  `sync_runs`, `sync_program_runs`, plus new fields on five existing collections and `is_unique` on
  every `clubspot_*_id`. Regenerated with `directus schema snapshot`, not hand-edited.
- **`just directus-local`** — Directus 12.3.1 and Postgres as containers with the CRM schema applied.
  Steps 4 through 10 tested against it.
- **SDK types** — `CustomField`'s attributes, and the participant fields the SDK was missing.
- **Deployment** — a `clubspot-sync` service account, a generated Directus token in Secret Manager,
  a least-privilege Directus role, a Dockerfile target, a Cloud Run job, and a six-hour schedule.

Merges #124, which restructured `packages/infrastructure` while this branch had renamed the file it
deleted.

## Two decisions worth a look

**Person identity resolves once, at row creation, and is never re-resolved.** That is what makes a
manual merge durable — staff repoint the FK, delete the duplicate, and no later sync reverts it. The
matcher is deliberately reluctant: a false split costs a staff minute, a false merge attaches one
family's medical and emergency data to another person. There is a regression test for this
(`person-sync.test.ts`).

**The sync cancels rather than deletes**, except `session_classes`, which is a pure join with no
status field. That exception is the only `delete` in the Directus permission rules.

## Corrected against live Clubspot data

The design's first draft trusted the SDK's types. Checking the real API (50 camps, 168 participants)
found three wrong: `weight` is a real participant field populated on 118 of 168, not a custom field;
`pcpName`/`pcpNumber` exist so the physician fields have a source; and emergency contacts do have an
email, though CYC has filled it once in 168.

## Not done here

- **Step 12 of the plan: deploy and verify.** Nothing has been applied. Needs
  `pulumi stack init prod --cwd ./packages/infrastructure/src/crm` first, since that project is new.
- **Notifications** — #122, including where `notifications.ts` should live.
- **The `sessions` capacity panel** — #123. Until it exists, that report row stays enabled.
- **`registrations` billing** is replaced; the remaining report rows are retired by a human setting
  `enabled` to false, no code change or deploy.

Also filed: #126, a gap where schema-apply verification checks collections but not relations, found
when a `PATCH /relations` silently dropped two FK constraints mid-session.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3

Failure: `queryCampEntries` filters only on `exists("confirmed_at")`, so an `applied` or `invited` registration writes `status: "applied"` — accepted by the varchar column, blank in the Directus dropdown, and invisible to any roster filter written against the three documented values. - `packages/clubspot-sync/src/registrations.ts:264-276`: billing is reconciled by `clubspot_billing_id`, while `registration_billing.registration_id` is `is_unique: true`. If Clubspot ever replaces a registration's billing object, the plan emits a create and Directus rejects it on the unique constraint, failing the camp.
- `packages/clubspot-sync/src/sync-run.ts:428-435`: anything that throws between `startRun` and the camp loop (`priorProgramRuns`, `discoverCamps`, `readSharedTables`) leaves the `sync_runs` row at `status: "running"` with no `error` — the one state the log can't explain.
- `packages/infrastructure/src/directus/resources.ts:292-308`: `DirectusUser`'s outputs are `{...inputs}`, so the new `token` lands in the dynamic resource's state with no `additionalSecretOutputs`. Same shape as the pre-existing `adminPassword`, so it may be an accepted trade — but the blast radius is now a credential Pulumi generated rather than one a human can rotate out of band.
- `packages/clubspot-sync/src/person-sync.ts:83-101`: candidates are fetched by email *or* last name, never both. A participant first synced without an email (person row stores `email: null`) will not appear in the email-keyed candidate set once Clubspot has one, so the next run creates a duplicate instead of filling the gap the design intends. This matches the design doc's wording, so it may be deliberate.</result>

Fix three duplicate Pulumi URNs introduced by the `clubspot-sync` infrastructure (commit `f56950e2`). Each aborts `pulumi up` at resource-registration time, before any diff is computed, so neither the `bootstrap` nor the `infrastructure` stack can currently apply. They were missed because the deploy step is deliberately deferred in this session.

All three are the same root cause: a resource name keyed on only one half of a pair.

## 1. `allowImpersonation` collides across service accounts

`packages/infrastructure/src/service-account.ts:18,24` names its two bindings `${member}-user` and `${member}-impersonator` — keyed on the member, with nothing identifying the service account.

`packages/infrastructure/src/bootstrap/report-runner.ts:12` already grants `user:ungood@onetrue.name`. `packages/infrastructure/src/bootstrap/clubspot-sync.ts:12` now grants the same member on a different account, in the same Pulumi project. Result: two resources named `user:ungood@onetrue.name-user`.

Fix by including the service account in the name. `ServiceAccount`'s constructor takes `accountId` as a plain string (`service-account.ts:6`), so it can be captured and used in a resource name — `this.name` cannot, since it is a `pulumi.Output`.

## 2. The Directus role and user share a name

`packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/directus-roles.ts:75` (a `DirectusRole`) and `:88` (a `DirectusUser`) are both named `"crm-clubspot-sync"`. Both extend `pulumi.dynamic.Resource` without a custom `module`/`type`, so both register under the single type token `pulumi-nodejs:dynamic:Resource` — identical type, identical name, identical URN.

The existing pairs avoid this only by accident: `crm-staff` versus `crm-staff-ungood`. Rename the user to follow that shape.

## 3. `Secret.grant()` collides across grantees

`packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/secret.ts:24` names the binding `secret-accessor-${this.plainId}` — keyed on the secret, not the grantee.

`run-reports-job.ts:26` grants `clubspot-username` and `clubspot-password` to `reportRunner`; `clubspot-sync-job.ts:22` grants the same two secrets to `clubspotSyncRunner`. Result: two resources named `secret-accessor-clubspot-username`, and two named `secret-accessor-clubspot-password`.

Reusing the existing secrets is correct and should stay — `grant()` simply cannot express two grantees today. Give it a way to. Note the member is a `pulumi.Input<string>` and may be an `Output`, so it cannot be interpolated into a resource name; the caller needs to supply a static label.

## Constraints

- **Renaming an existing resource means Pulumi deletes and recreates it.** That is acceptable here — these are IAM bindings, and recreation is harmless — but say so in the commit message so the first apply's diff isn't a surprise. Do not add `pulumi.Alias`; the user has explicitly declined aliasing for this work.
- Keep the fix to the naming. Do not change what any binding grants, to whom, or on what.
- `service-account.ts` and `secret.ts` are shared helpers used by existing resources. Update every call site.
- Do NOT touch `packages/clubspot-sync`, `packages/crm/schema.yaml`, or `docs/`.
- Do NOT run `pulumi up`, `just deploy`, or `just deploy-bootstrap`.

## Acceptance

- `just ci` passes.
- No two resources in the same Pulumi project share a name, for `bootstrap`, `infrastructure`, and `crm`. Check this by reading the resource names each project registers, not by running Pulumi — you cannot apply from here.
- Report the full list of resource names that change, since those become delete-and-recreate on the next apply.

Commit once.

content.text:
The review found real problems. **Don't merge #128 yet — it cannot deploy.**

## Blocking (3) — fix running now

Three duplicate Pulumi URNs, all the same root cause: a resource name keyed on half a pair. Each aborts `pulumi up` at registration time, before any diff. I verified all three against the source.

Nothing caught them because step 12 is deferred — there's no automated gate between `just ci` and a live apply.

## High (3) — real, not yet fixed

**Silent truncation.** `main.ts:42` calls `queryCampEntries(camp).find()` with no limit, so Parse returns at most 100. Every other registration query in the repo sets `.limit(1000)` explicitly. A camp with 140 registrations syncs 100, logs `status: "ok"`, and **advances its watermark** — so the missing 40 are never retried. Silent, permanent data loss. `discoverCamps` has the same shape, and you have ~50 camps.

**Medical data is write-once.** `person-sync.ts:154` reuses `fillGapsPatch` for `medical_profiles`, so only null columns are ever written. Fill-gaps-only exists to protect a *staff edit* on `people` — but Clubspot is the sole source of truth for medical data. A guardian updating allergies from `"peanuts"` to `"peanuts, bee stings"` never reaches the CRM, and the roster staff read in an emergency is the stale one. A retracted medication is equally sticky.

**Participants are re-matched every run.** `registrations.person_id` is correctly pinned, but `syncParticipant` still runs the full matcher for every participant, then writes contacts and medical profiles against whatever it resolves *now* — never consulting the registration's existing `person_id`. Fix a name spelling in Clubspot and you get an orphan person holding the fresh medical profile while the registration still points at the old one. This is the invariant I briefed hardest on, and it's half-implemented.

## Medium (4) — two are disclosure

**`main.ts:87` logs the Directus token** at debug level via `options: action.opts()`. Copied from `admin-functions`, but the static token is new and rotating it means a Pulumi apply.

**`directus.ts:118` dry-run logs the whole patch** — including `allergies`, `medications`, `conditions`. The design's own rollout step is "the first production run is a dry run," which would write a minor's medical record into Cloud Logging, outside the permission model `medical_profiles` exists to enforce. `createItems` gets this right and logs a count only.

Plus: the registration watermark is passed but dropped by the only implementation (`main.ts:30`), so every camp re-reads everything every run — and the README documents filtering that doesn't happen. And `registration_entries.status` can write `"applied"` or `""` into a column documented and configured as a three-value enum.

**My recommendation:** fix blocking + all three High + the two logging ones before merge. The watermark and status-vocabulary findings can be issues. Want me to keep going through them?

The blast radius is bigger than expected — since `Secret.grant` now requires a label everywhere, this renames existing secret-accessor bindings across substrate/directus/portal too, so the first apply will show around 18 delete+creates. It's harmless recreation of IAM bindings, but I'm worried about a brief window during apply where the substrate VM's SA loses secret access while bindings are being recreated.

Actually, since the substrate VM only reads secrets at boot rather than continuously, a running VM wouldn't be affected — this is acceptable.

Now I want to move on to fixing the High findings, since the user's kept saying to keep going. I'm considering splitting the work across agents: one handling query limits, participant re-matching, and the dropped watermark issue (all related to query/resolution correctness in main.ts/person-sync.ts), and another handling medical write-once logic plus the logging issues around secrets/PII. Since only one writer can work at a time, I'll do these sequentially, starting with the medical staleness fix since it's the highest priority.

Given #4 is silent data loss and #6 creates orphan records, I think it makes more sense to bundle #4, #5, #6, and #7 into a single agent since they're all interrelated correctness issues living in clubspot-sync/src, touching main.ts, sync-run.ts, and person-sync.ts. Then a second agent can tackle the logging issues (#8, #9) in main.ts and directus.ts separately.

For the #6 fix specifically, I'm working out that syncParticipant needs to reuse an existing registration's person_id when one already exists, only doing a fresh match on creation — which means restructuring the run loop so PersonSync happens after looking up existing registrations by clubspot_registration_id, rather than before planRegistrations as it currently does.

For #5, I'm reasoning that medical_profiles should be a full overwrite rather than fill-gaps, since Clubspot is the source of truth there even though the general design protects staff edits elsewhere — medical data is the exception. For #4 I'll add explicit row limits matching the repo's existing convention, and for #7 I'll implement watermark filtering directly in the gateway. Now I'm ready to write up the brief for this batch.

input.prompt:
Fix four review findings in `packages/clubspot-sync`. All four are real bugs found by review of the session branch; three of them lose or corrupt data silently. The design doc is `.claude/plans/clubspot-directus-sync.md`.

## 1. Unbounded Parse queries silently truncate at 100 rows

`packages/clubspot-sync/src/main.ts:42` calls `queryCampEntries(camp).find()` with no limit. Parse's default page size is 100. Every other registration query in this repo sets it explicitly — `admin-functions/src/participants.ts:108`, `contacts.ts:60`, `sessions.ts:69` all use `.limit(1000)`.

**Failure:** a camp with 140 confirmed registrations syncs 100. No error is raised, the camp is logged `status: "ok"`, and its watermark advances — so the missing 40 are never retried. Silent, permanent.

`packages/clubspot-sync/src/camps.ts:10` (`discoverCamps`) and the other `find()` calls in `main.ts` have the same shape. Audit every `.find()` in the package and give each an explicit bound.

A hard cap that silently drops row 1001 is only a better failure than one that drops row 101. Decide whether to page or to fail loudly when a result hits the cap, and say which you chose and why. Do not leave a limit that can truncate without anyone noticing.

## 2. Medical data is write-once

`packages/clubspot-sync/src/person-sync.ts:154-171` reuses `fillGapsPatch` for `medical_profiles`, so only `null` columns are ever written.

Fill-gaps-only is deliberate for `people` — it protects a staff edit, and a merge, from being clobbered by the next registration naming that person. content.content:
### What the job syncs, and when

There is no config collection and no `enabled` toggle. The job syncs everything for one club. The
club id comes from a `CLUBSPOT_CLUB_ID` environment variable on the Cloud Run job, the same shape
as `CONFIG_SPREADSHEET_ID` today (`run-reports-job.ts:78`) and already an established variable name
in the SDK CLI (`packages/clubspot-sdk/src/main.ts:128`).

Each run:

1. List every non-archived `Camp` for the club, as `camps.ts:37` already does.
2. For each camp, decide whether anything changed since that camp's own watermark. A camp's
   `updatedAt` does not move when a child object changes, so the camp is checked with one
   `Parse.Query.count()` per child class, each filtered on `updatedAt >= watermark`: `CampSession`,
   `CampClass`, `Registration`, and `RegistrationCampSession`. If every count is zero and the
   camp's own `updatedAt` is older than the watermark, skip the camp.
3. Sync each camp that changed, and record one log row per camp.

Two known holes in step 2, both closed by the same rule:

- `EntryCap` has no pointer to a camp (`packages/clubspot-sdk/src/types.ts:338-342`), so a
  capacity-only change is invisible to the count queries.
- Nothing in Clubspot's `updatedAt` reveals a delete.

So any camp whose last successful sync is more than 24 hours old is synced regardless of the
counts. That is a refresh floor, not a snooze.

**Snooze is premature.** The cost the user is worried about is four `count()` calls per camp per
run. With tens of camps and an hourly schedule that is a few hundred cheap queries a day, against
the thousands of object reads a full pass costs. Add a snooze when a measurement says it is needed.

### The sync log

content.text:
Design doc updated for both (`f402a74c`). Here's where things stand.

**Blocking URN fix landed** (`61ad76b2`). Worth knowing: the blast radius is wider than the three collisions. `Secret.grant()` now requires a grantee label at every call site, so **~18 IAM bindings get destroyed and recreated** on the first apply — including `substrate-runner`'s secret accessors for the Directus key, DB password, and OAuth client. All IAM bindings, all harmless to recreate, but your first `just deploy` diff will be noisier than you'd expect for a "naming" fix.

**Your two PR comments are queued, not ignored.** Comment 2 moves the row interfaces out of `registrations.ts` and friends — the exact files the correctness fix is writing to right now. Dispatching a second writer would collide, so they go next.

On **comment 1**, I think you're right and the design doc now says so. Dropping the counts also lets me retire two blind spots I'd papered over with the floor rather than fixed: `EntryCap` has no camp pointer so capacity changes were invisible, and nothing in `updatedAt` reveals a delete. Both stop mattering when a due run is a full reconcile. The backoff state needs **no schema change** — `sync_program_runs` already records `items_created`/`items_updated`, so consecutive zero-write runs are a read of the log.

On **comment 2**, `packages/crm` today is just `schema.yaml` and a README with no `src`. Making it a real TypeScript package is the right destination and means `clubspot-sync` ends up declaring no entity types at all — Clubspot's side already lives in `clubspot-sdk`.

Queued in order once the running fix lands: row types to `crm`, then backoff. I'll do the type move first, since backoff rewrites `change-detection.ts` and I'd rather not move types through a file that's being deleted.

input.prompt:
Fix two disclosure findings from review of `packages/clubspot-sync`. Both write sensitive data into Cloud Logging, where it outlives the run and is readable by anyone with log access.

## 1. The Directus static token is logged at debug level

`packages/clubspot-sync/src/main.ts:87-90`'s `preAction` hook logs `options: action.opts()`, which dumps every resolved option. That now includes `--directus-token` and `--password`.

The pattern was copied from `packages/admin-functions/src/main.ts:42`, where it was already questionable, but the Directus static token is new and worse: it is long-lived, it is Pulumi-generated, and rotating it means a Pulumi apply. One `--verbose debug` run in Cloud Run puts it in the log permanently.

CLAUDE.md and #49 both record that secrets must not be exposed this way. Keep the debug line — knowing which action ran with which options is genuinely useful — but redact the secret-bearing options rather than dropping the log entirely.

Do NOT change `admin-functions/src/main.ts`. It has the same shape and the same problem, but it is out of scope here; report it and I will file an issue.

## 2. Dry-run logs a minor's medical record

`packages/clubspot-sync/src/directus.ts:118` logs the whole `patch` in `updateItem`'s dry-run branch. For `medical_profiles` that is `conditions`, `allergies`, `medications`, and physician contact.

The design doc's own rollout step is "the first production run is a dry run" — so the recommended first action writes minors' medical data to stderr and Cloud Logging, entirely outside the permission model `medical_profiles` exists to enforce.

`createItems` already gets this right: it logs a collection and a count, no values (`directus.ts:109`). `deleteItem` logs an id, which is fine. Make `updateItem` consistent with `createItems`.

A dry run still has to be useful for verifying what would change, so log enough to audit — the collection, the row id, and which fields would be written — without the values themselves. Field *names* are schema, not data.

## Scope fence

- `packages/clubspot-sync/src/main.ts` and `src/directus.ts` only, plus tests.
- Do NOT modify `packages/admin-functions`.
- Do NOT change what is written to Directus, only what is logged.
- Do NOT touch the plan functions, `person-sync.ts`, `sync-run.ts`, or `packages/infrastructure`.

## Tests

- The debug log does not contain the token or the Clubspot password.
- A dry-run `updateItem` on `medical_profiles` logs the field names but none of the values.

The existing tests stub `fetch` and are in `packages/clubspot-sync/test/`. For the logging assertions, spy on winston rather than reaching into transports.

## Acceptance

- `just ci` passes.
- Grepping the package for a log call that passes a whole options object or a whole patch turns up nothing.

Commit once.

input.description: Move CRM row types into crm package
input.prompt:
Act on a PR review comment on #128. The reviewer (the repo owner) said, on `packages/clubspot-sync/src/registrations.ts:31`:

> These "row" interfaces do not belong in clubspot-sync. Either they describe clubspot entities, in which case they should be in the clubspot-sdk package or they represent directus entities, which then they belong in the app built on directus (crm, for example).
>
> The point of a sync job is to map from one schema to another, not define its own schema.

They are Directus entities, so they move to `packages/crm`. The design doc records this at its "Where the CRM's row types live" section.

## Task

**Make `packages/crm` a TypeScript package.** Today it is only `schema.yaml`, a `README.md`, and a `package.json` with no build. Give it the same shape as the other library packages — `packages/commodore` is the smallest model: `tsconfig.json` extending `../../tsconfig.json` with `rootDir: "./src"` / `outDir: "./dist"`, and `package.json` gaining `type`, `main`, `types`, `files`, and the `prepare`/`build`/`clean` scripts.

**Move every CRM row interface** out of `packages/clubspot-sync/src` and into `packages/crm/src`, exported from its index. They are spread across:

- `people.ts` — `PersonRow`, `ContactRow`, `MedicalProfileRow`
- `schedule.ts` — `ProgramRow`, `SessionRow`, `ClassRow`, `SessionClassRow`, `EntryCapRow`

### Dependency Graph

`crm`, `portal`, and `substrate` are apps deployed by `infrastructure`, not TypeScript libraries
other packages import — they have no `@cyc-seattle/*` dependencies of their own.

```
commodore (base utilities)
    ↑
    ├── clubspot-sdk (Parse SDK wrapper for TheClubSpot API)
    │       ↑
    │       ├── admin-functions (reports, participants, camps, sessions)
    │       ├── todo-manager (Todoist integration)
    │       └── clubspot-sync (Directus sync for the CRM — no gsuite dependency, by design)
    │
gsuite (Google Workspace API wrappers)
```

input.prompt:
Act on a PR review comment on #128. The reviewer (the repo owner) said, on `packages/clubspot-sync/src/change-detection.ts:62`:

> I don't really like this change detection mechanism, as a) most of the work is in querying clubspot, which has to be done to get the childCounts anyway and b) it will continue to sync a camp indefinitely at least once a day.
>
> Instead, I want an exponential backoff approach: start by syncing every time the job runs, but if there are no changes for a particular entity being synced - backoff by some reasonable percent - to a maximum of once a week.

The design doc's "What the job syncs, and when" section has been rewritten to match; read it — it is the specification.

## What goes away

`packages/clubspot-sync/src/change-detection.ts` in its current form. Both halves of it are wrong:

- `countChildChanges` issues four `Parse.Query.count()` calls per camp per run, hitting the same classes a sync would read anyway. They cost about what fetching costs and buy almost nothing.
- `needsSync`'s `REFRESH_FLOOR_MS` forces a full sync of every camp every 24 hours, so a camp that finished in 2024 and can never change again is resynced daily, forever.

Delete both, and the `watermarkForCamp` plumbing if the backoff replaces its role. Their tests go with them.

## What replaces it

Per-camp exponential backoff, decided from the sync log:

- A camp starts syncing on every run.
- A sync that writes nothing backs the camp off — roughly doubling its interval.
- A sync that writes something resets it to every run.
- The interval caps at one week.

**No schema change.** `sync_program_runs` already records `items_created` and `items_updated` per camp per run, so "how many consecutive runs wrote nothing" is a read of the log the run loop already performs (`sync-run.ts` reads prior program runs once per run). The interval is a function of that count; a camp is due when `now - last_sync_start >= interval`.

Keep the decision a **pure function over plain data**, the way `needsSync` was — that is the one thing about the old design worth preserving. Something like "given this camp's ordered prior runs and this clock, is it due, and what is its interval". The executor stays thin.

Pick the base interval, the growth factor, and how you count a "wrote nothing" run, and justify each in a short comment. The job runs every six hours; the cap is one week. Note that `skipped` rows are not sync attempts and must not count as either changed or unchanged — only actual syncs move the backoff.

## Two things this simplifies — verify, don't assume

The old design had a "two known holes" note, both papered over by the refresh floor:

- `EntryCap` has no pointer to a camp, so a capacity-only change was invisible to the count queries.
- Nothing in Clubspot's `updatedAt` reveals a delete.

Neither should matter now, because a due run is a full reconcile of the camp's schedule rather than something that must detect a change first. Confirm that is actually true of the current code — that a due camp re-reads and reconciles sessions, classes, session_classes and entry caps unconditionally — rather than taking it on faith. If some part of the sync still depends on change detection having happened, say so.

## Interaction with the registration watermark

Registrations are still filtered on `updatedAt` between the camp's watermark and the run start — that is separate from the backoff and stays. Make sure the watermark still advances correctly when a camp is synced after a long backoff: the window must cover everything since the last *successful* sync, not since the last run.

This is the subtle one. A camp backed off to weekly that then syncs must not miss registrations created during the backoff.

## Tests

- A camp with no prior runs is due.
- A camp whose last sync wrote something is due on the next run.
- Consecutive zero-write syncs lengthen the interval.
- The interval never exceeds a week.
- A sync that writes something resets the interval.
- `skipped` rows do not affect the backoff.
- A camp synced after a long backoff uses a watermark covering the whole gap.

## Scope fence

- `packages/clubspot-sync` only, plus `packages/clubspot-sync/README.md` (it documents the 24-hour refresh floor, which is going away).
- Do NOT change `packages/crm`, `packages/crm/schema.yaml`, `docs/`, or `packages/infrastructure`. The backoff needs no new column — if you conclude it does, stop and report rather than changing the schema.
- Do NOT change the Cloud Run schedule.
- Do NOT touch `packages/clubspot-sdk` or `packages/admin-functions`.

## Acceptance

- `just ci` passes.
- No `Parse.Query.count()` remains in the package.
- The backoff decision is a pure function with direct unit tests.
- A camp that syncs and writes nothing is not synced again on the very next run.

Report the base interval and factor you chose, and whether the two "known holes" really are closed.

Commit once.

**Row types moved** (`2e443248`), and it proved the change rather than assuming it: built both Docker targets, then ran the image and dynamically imported the compiled modules *inside the container* to confirm `@cyc-seattle/crm` resolves at runtime. It also diffed all 14 types against `schema.yaml` field-by-field with `js-yaml`. `clubspot-sync` now declares no entity types of its own.

One thing it noticed and correctly didn't "fix": several `clubspot_*_id` columns are nullable in the DB but non-null in the TS types. That's deliberate — the DB permits null for a hypothetical row the sync didn't create, but the sync always populates them. Loosening the types to match the DB would weaken an invariant the code actually holds.

I folded in the two doc consequences (`0d155a69`): `crm` is now a library as well as an app, so the dependency graph's claim that it has no consumers was wrong.

**Backoff is running now** — the last of your two comments. Points I pushed on in the brief:

- **`skipped` rows must not move the backoff.** Only actual sync attempts count as changed or unchanged, or a camp that's skipped for being backed off would keep backing itself off.
- **Verify, don't assume, that the two "known holes" close.** The old design had `EntryCap` having no camp pointer, and deletes being invisible to `updatedAt`, both papered over by the refresh floor. They *should* stop mattering when a due run is a full reconcile — but only if the schedule pass really is unconditional. I asked it to confirm that in the code rather than take it from the doc.
- **The subtle one: the watermark after a long backoff.** A camp backed off to weekly must sync a window covering the whole gap, not just since the last run, or registrations created during the backoff vanish silently.

**Design chosen:**

Both PR comments are addressed now, but I want to scrutinize the agent's honest flag: a failing camp backs off exponentially just like an idle one, with no way to distinguish them from the log alone. That seems like a real design flaw—a persistently broken camp would get checked less and less, eventually only weekly, when arguably it should be retried more aggressively instead of backed off.

The user's stated semantics were "no changes → back off," but a failure isn't "no changes," it's "unknown state." The agent's `recordProgramRun` treats failed rows the same as empty ones, but it doesn't have to—`status` distinguishes `failed` from `ok`, so failures could be excluded from the backoff count entirely, or treated as a reset to promptly retry rather than delay recovery for up to a week. Given the job runs every 6 hours and failures already surface as non-zero exits that Cloud Run would flag, I lean toward retrying promptly on failure rather than backing off, since exponential backoff mainly protects against hammering a broken target but here that risk seems lower than the cost of delayed recovery.

The right semantics: a failure should leave the interval unchanged rather than lengthening it, so only a successful sync that wrote nothing counts as "no changes." A camp at weekly that starts failing stays weekly, and one at 6h that fails just retries at 6h — both correct behaviors.

This is small enough to fix inline rather than dispatching: just changing the empty-run predicate to only count `ok` rows, plus a test. Let me look at backoff.ts first.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reconciles Pulumi state with what actually exists, for both projects. Changes no resource, but
# it does rewrite state, so out-of-band edits (e.g. a permission row changed directly in Directus)
# show up as a diff on the next deploy rather than silently.
set -euo pipefail

here="$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")"
"$here/pulumi-tunnel" refresh --yes
exec pulumi refresh --yes --cwd "$here/../packages/infrastructure/src/crm" --stack "${PULUMI_STACK:-prod}"
════ preview ════
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shows the diff `just deploy` would apply to both projects, without applying it.
set -euo pipefail

here="$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")"
"$here/pulumi-tunnel" preview
exec pulumi preview --cwd "$here/../packages/infrastructure/src/crm" --stack "${PULUMI_STACK:-prod}"

**The four fixes landed first** (`a6b07cb8`), so this deploy includes them — 213 tests:

- **`registration_entries.status`** normalizes to the three documented values, warning on `applied`/`invited`/blank rather than writing them into a column nothing can filter.

On your backfill use case, the flag reasoning is sound: `--since` only moves the registration query's lower bound. The schedule pass is already a full reconcile every run, so nothing else needed changing. And the watermark isn't special-cased on write — the query's upper bound is always "now", so a run that completes has by construction covered everything through now, and the next ordinary run picks up cleanly.

So your verify-and-backfill path is:

```
clubspot-sync --camp <id> --since 2024-01-01 --dry-run   # check first
clubspot-sync --camp <id> --since 2024-01-01             # then commit
```

One thing it flagged worth a later look: `registrations.status` — the raw registration-level string, distinct from the entry status — still writes `""` when Clubspot has none. `docs/crm-schema.md` documents that column as free-text pass-through, so it's not the same bug, but an empty string in a NOT NULL column is untidy.

content.text:
First deploy attempt failed. Two causes, and one of them was my mistake.

**#124's code had never actually been run.** `directus-roles.ts:1` and `crm/index.ts:11` imported `"../directus/index.js"` — the only two imports in the package carrying a `.js` suffix. Pulumi runs the program through its vendored ts-node in **CommonJS** mode, which resolves that path literally, and only `index.ts` exists on disk. The stack died with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` before computing a diff. That came in with #124 and nothing had exercised it, since its apply was deliberately held. Fixed in `17827f68`.

**I skipped `just deploy-bootstrap`.** The new `clubspot-sync` service account lives in the bootstrap stack, and `just deploy` only applies infrastructure and crm. So `identities.ts:30` read an output that didn't exist yet and crashed on `undefined.email`. The design doc says this explicitly and I went straight to `just deploy` anyway.

Bootstrap is now applied — 7 created, 4 deleted, matching the IAM renames. Main deploy is running.

One thing worth fixing afterwards: `identities.ts:20` uses `getOutput`, so a missing stack output surfaces as `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'email')`. `crm/refs.ts:14` already uses `requireOutput` for exactly this reason, with a comment saying so — it fails naming the output instead. Worth making `identities.ts` match, since that error cost more to diagnose than it should have.

content.text:
Third failure, third real bug — and this one's genuinely interesting.

**Infrastructure largely applied** (13 created, 2 updated), then the Cloud Run job creation failed:

```
Error waiting to create Job: ... Image '.../clubspot-sync:latest' not found.
```

The job's `image` field is `pulumi.concat(artifactRepositoryUrl, "/", imageName)` — a plain string that never references the `docker.Image` resource. So **Pulumi sees no dependency edge** between the job and its image, and is free to create the job first, against a tag that doesn't exist yet.

`run-reports-job.ts` has the identical shape. It has never failed only because its image is already in the registry, so the ordering has never mattered. I fixed both (`8d1d2c5f`) rather than leave a trap for the next new job or a registry rebuild.

Deploying again.

Worth noting the pattern across these three failures: every one was invisible to `just ci`. Type-checking, linting, and 213 unit tests all pass on code that cannot load under Pulumi's CommonJS ts-node, and on a resource graph with a missing edge. `just preview` catches the first class cheaply and I should have reached for it before the first deploy rather than after the second.

One thing I changed after review: the first implementation counted a **failed** run as "nothing changed", so a camp erroring every run would double its own retry interval until it was being attempted once a week. A transient Clubspot fault or a data shape the mapping rejects would make the sync quietly give up on it. A failure now resets the due timer without lengthening the interval — it means "we don't know", not "nothing changed".
EOF

input.command:
gh pr edit 128 --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Issues #69 and #70. Clubspot data now syncs into the CRM's Directus instance instead of Google
Sheets tabs, and the job decides what to sync from camp discovery plus a sync log rather than a
config spreadsheet.

Design doc: `.claude/plans/clubspot-directus-sync.md`.

## What's here

- **`people-hub` renamed to `crm`** — the package, the doc, the Pulumi project, and the resource
  names. Roles are recreated rather than aliased: the CRM holds no data and its stack had never been
  initialized.
- **`packages/clubspot-sync`** — reads Clubspot, writes the CRM through Directus's REST API. Pure
  plan functions plus thin executors, so the mapping is unit-testable with no Directus and no Parse.
- **`packages/crm` is now a TypeScript package** exporting the row types for the schema it owns, so
  the sync declares no entity types of its own.
- **Schema changes** — `registration_billing`, `custom_field_definitions`, `custom_field_responses`,
  `sync_runs`, `sync_program_runs`, new fields on five existing collections, and `is_unique` on every
  `clubspot_*_id`. Regenerated with `directus schema snapshot`.
- **`just directus-local`** — Directus 12.3.1 and Postgres as containers with the CRM schema applied.
- **SDK types** — `CustomField`'s attributes and the participant fields the SDK was missing.
- **Deployment** — a `clubspot-sync` service account, a generated Directus token in Secret Manager,
  a least-privilege Directus role, a Dockerfile target, a Cloud Run job, and a six-hour schedule.

Merges #124, which restructured `packages/infrastructure` while this branch had renamed the file it
deleted.

## Review feedback, all addressed

Both inline comments are answered on their threads.

- **Change detection replaced with per-camp exponential backoff.** No `count()` queries; the 24-hour
  refresh floor is gone. Backing off also retired the two blind spots that floor existed to cover.
- **Row types moved to `packages/crm`.**

A read-only review pass found ten more, since fixed:

- **Three duplicate Pulumi URNs** that aborted both stacks at registration time. `allowImpersonation`
  and `Secret.grant` each named resources after one half of a pair.
- **Silent truncation at 100 rows.** An unbounded `.find()` synced 100 of a camp's 140 registrations,
  logged `ok`, and advanced the watermark, so the rest were never retried. Now paged.
- **Medical data was write-once.** `medical_profiles` reused fill-gaps-only, so an updated allergy
  never propagated and a retracted medication never cleared.
- **Participants were re-matched every run**, producing orphan people holding fresh medical data while
  the registration still pointed at the old row.

content.text:
Deploy's still running (8 pulumi processes), output buffered, so I can't pull build timings from it yet. But the cause is clear, and it's two things compounding.

**1. Every image is cross-compiled under emulation.** Your Mac is arm64; all three images declare `linux/amd64` because Cloud Run and the substrate VM are amd64. So every build runs through QEMU in a VM with 2 CPUs and 4 GB. `tsc` is CPU-bound and suffers badly — 5–20× native is typical.

**2. The Dockerfile invalidates its own install layer on every source change.** It copies all the package sources *before* `pnpm install`:

```
COPY packages/admin-functions/ packages/admin-functions/
COPY packages/clubspot-sdk/ ...
...
RUN pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --filter=...
```

Change one line in `clubspot-sync` and that `COPY` layer busts, so `pnpm install` re-runs from scratch. And per the Dockerfile's own comment at line 19, install runs every workspace package's `prepare` — which is `tsc --build`. So each image build recompiles `calendar-sync` and `todo-manager` too, packages that never enter the image, under emulation.

The pnpm store cache mount saves the *downloads*, but not the linking or the compiling, which is the expensive part.

**Two fixes, very different effort:**

**Bump the podman VM** — no code change, probably the biggest single win. 2 CPUs is unusually low for emulated builds:

```
podman machine stop && podman machine set --cpus 8 --memory 8192 && podman machine start
```

Don't run that right now — it would kill the in-flight deploy.

**Restructure the Dockerfile** to the standard pnpm pattern: copy only the `package.json` files and lockfile, `pnpm install --ignore-scripts`, *then* copy sources and build explicitly. That makes the dependency layer cache across source-only changes, which is nearly every build. More involved, since `prepare` currently does the compiling.

Longer term, #118's GitHub Actions deploy would sidestep emulation entirely by building natively on amd64 — worth weighing against restructuring the Dockerfile, since that work is coming anyway.

Want me to file the Dockerfile one as an issue? It's a real, durable fix, and it's out of scope for this PR.

input.command:
gh issue create --title "Stop emulating tsc: build natively and cache the install layer" --label "docker,P2" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Problem

Local deploys spend most of their time in the Docker build, and almost all of that is avoidable.

Two causes compound.

**1. Every image is cross-compiled under emulation.** The dev machine is arm64; all three images
declare `platforms: ["linux/amd64"]` (`clubspot-sync-job.ts:37`, `run-reports-job.ts:45`,
`substrate.ts:59`) because Cloud Run and the substrate VM are amd64. So the whole build — including
`tsc` — runs through QEMU inside the podman VM. Emulation typically costs 5-20x native, and `tsc` is
exactly the CPU-bound work that suffers most.

**2. The Dockerfile invalidates its own install layer on every source change.** It copies all package
sources before installing:

```
COPY packages/admin-functions/ packages/admin-functions/
COPY packages/clubspot-sdk/ packages/clubspot-sdk/
COPY packages/clubspot-sync/ packages/clubspot-sync/
...
RUN pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --filter=...
```

Change one line in any package and that COPY layer busts, so `pnpm install` re-runs from scratch. Per
the Dockerfile's own comment at `:19`, install runs every workspace package's `prepare`, which is
`tsc --build` — so each image build also recompiles `calendar-sync` and `todo-manager`, packages whose
source never enters the image. The pnpm store cache mount saves the downloads, not the linking or the
compiling.

## Fix

**Run the build stage on the native architecture.** BuildKit's `$BUILDPLATFORM` lets the build stage
match the host while the runtime stage stays amd64:

```dockerfile
FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM node:22-alpine AS build
...
FROM node:22-alpine AS clubspot-sync      # still linux/amd64
COPY --from=build /usr/app/clubspot-sync /usr/app/clubspot-sync
```

This is safe here because `tsc` emits architecture-neutral JavaScript and the production dependency
trees are pure JS. The only native modules in the repo are dev tooling —
`lightningcss-darwin-arm64`, `@rolldown/binding-darwin-arm64`, and `fsevents`, all vitest/vite
devDependencies, none of which reach a runtime image. Confirm that still holds before landing, since
it is the assumption the whole approach rests on.

**Reorder the Dockerfile so the dependency layer caches.** Copy the workspace manifests and lockfile,
install with `--ignore-scripts`, then copy sources and build explicitly. That keeps install cached
across source-only changes, which is nearly every build. It needs untangling `prepare` from install,
since `prepare` is what currently does the compiling.

**Also worth doing, no code change:** the podman machine is provisioned with 2 CPUs and 4 GB, which is
low for builds of this size even natively.

```sh
podman machine stop
podman machine set --cpus 8 --memory 8192
podman machine start
```

## Impact

Only local deploys. Once #118 moves deploys to GitHub Actions, builds run natively on amd64 and the
emulation cost disappears on its own — so weigh the Dockerfile work against how soon that lands. The
layer-ordering fix and the podman bump help regardless.

Not a correctness issue: the images that come out today are correct, just slow to produce.

## Note on the alternative

Building outside the container and copying `dist/` in was considered and rejected. `.dockerignore`
excludes `**/dist` and `**/node_modules` deliberately — its comment says they are "recreated inside
the image; excluded so an explicit `COPY packages/<name>/` doesn't sweep in a local build's
artifacts." Copying host artifacts in would make the image no longer derivable from its build context,
so a stale or wrong-branch `dist` could ship silently. The native build stage gets the same speed
without giving that up.
EOF
)"

Implement issue #129: stop emulating `tsc` in the Docker build, and make the dependency layer cache. Run `gh issue view 129` — it has the full diagnosis, the chosen approach, and the alternative that was already considered and rejected.

You are in an isolated worktree. A production deploy is running concurrently in another worktree off the same podman machine.

## Two hard constraints

**Never run `podman machine stop`, `set`, or `start`.** The issue mentions bumping the VM's CPUs and memory as a separate no-code-change step. That is for a human to do later. Restarting the machine would kill the running deploy.

**Expect build contention.** The podman VM has 2 CPUs and is already running emulated builds for that deploy. Your test builds will be slow and will slow theirs. Build when you need evidence, not to browse.

## The work

**1. Native build stage.** Change the `build` stage to `FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM node:22-alpine AS build` so it runs on the host's architecture instead of under QEMU. The runtime stages (`report-runner`, `clubspot-sync`) stay `linux/amd64`.

This is safe only because `tsc` emits architecture-neutral JavaScript and the production dependency trees are pure JS. **Verify that assumption before relying on it** — it is the thing the whole approach rests on. Check the pruned production trees, not the whole workspace: the `.node` files present in `node_modules` today (`lightningcss-darwin-arm64`, `@rolldown/binding-darwin-arm64`, `fsevents`) are all vitest/vite devDependencies and should not appear in what `pnpm deploy --prod` produces. Say how you checked.

**2. Layer ordering.** Copy the workspace manifests and lockfile, install, then copy sources and build. Right now every package's source is copied before `pnpm install`, so any source change busts the install layer and re-runs `prepare` — which is `tsc --build` — for every workspace package, including `calendar-sync` and `todo-manager`, whose source never enters either image.

Untangling this means separating install from compile: `pnpm install --ignore-scripts` for the dependency layer, then an explicit build after the sources are copied. Keep the existing `pnpm deploy --prod` pruning for the runtime stages.

Preserve the `--mount=type=cache,id=pnpm` store mount, and keep the comment at `:24-25` explaining why the manifest-only COPYs exist (#114) — that constraint has not changed.

## Verification

A faster build that produces a broken image is worthless, so prove both stages still work:

- `docker build --target report-runner .` and `docker build --target clubspot-sync .` both succeed. Use `DOCKER_HOST` from `./scripts/podman-docker-host`.
- Each image actually runs: `node ./dist/main.js --help` inside each container. A missing module from mis-pruned production deps will not show up any other way.
- Confirm the final images are still `linux/amd64` — `docker image inspect` reports architecture. The whole point is that only the build stage changes platform.
- Measure. Record a rough before and after for a **source-only change** (touch a file in `clubspot-sync`, rebuild), since that is the case the layer ordering is meant to fix. A number in the commit message is worth more than a claim.

## Scope fence

- The root `Dockerfile`, and `.dockerignore` only if the reordering genuinely requires it — say why if so.
- Do NOT change `packages/infrastructure`. The `platforms: ["linux/amd64"]` on each `docker.Image` stays; the runtime images must remain amd64.
- Do NOT change any package's `package.json` scripts unless separating `prepare` from install requires it. If it does, keep `just build` and `just ci` working exactly as now.
- Do NOT build outside the container and copy `dist/` in. The issue explains why that was rejected.
- Do NOT touch `packages/clubspot-sync`, `packages/crm`, or anything under `docs/`.

## Acceptance

- `just ci` passes.
- Both images build, run, and report `linux/amd64`.
- A source-only rebuild no longer re-runs `pnpm install`.

Report the measured before/after and how you verified the production trees are pure JS.

Commit once.

input.description: Fix substrate image and speed up builds
input.prompt:
Two related pieces of work on this repo's Docker builds: a bug that currently breaks `just deploy`, and issue #129's performance work. Run `gh issue view 129` for the latter — it has the full diagnosis and the alternative already considered and rejected.

No deploy is running now, so podman is free. Work in the current worktree (branch `session/clubspot-directus`) — it has `packages/clubspot-sync`, which `main` does not.

## 1. The substrate image cannot build (fix this first)

`just deploy` fails with:

```
failed to compute cache key: failed to calculate checksum of ref ...:
"/packages/portal/dist/site": not found
```

`packages/substrate/Dockerfile` does `COPY packages/portal/dist/site /srv`, with the build context set to the repo root (`infrastructure/src/substrate.ts`'s `context: { location: "../../../.." }`). The root `.dockerignore` excludes `**/dist`, so that path is stripped from the context and the COPY can never resolve. The directory does exist on disk — it is purely a context-exclusion problem.

`git log -S'**/dist' -- .dockerignore` shows the exclusion arrived with #124 (`42944fb1`). The substrate image has not been rebuilt since, which is why nothing surfaced it.

`.dockerignore`'s own comment says dist is "recreated inside the image". That is true of the root `Dockerfile`, where `report-runner` and `clubspot-sync` compile internally — but not of `packages/substrate/Dockerfile`, whose header says the portal's site "is expected to be built already". One rule, right for one Dockerfile, silently wrong for the other.

**Fix it by making the substrate image self-contained**, consistent with what `.dockerignore` already assumes: build the portal inside the image in an earlier stage, then copy `dist/site` into the Caddy stage. The portal's build is `tsc --build && node dist/build.js` (`packages/portal/package.json`), so that stage needs Node and the portal package with its workspace dependencies.

Do NOT fix this by negating the `.dockerignore` exclusion. That would leave the image dependent on host build state — the exact fragility the exclusion exists to prevent, and the reason #129 rejected the copy-artifacts-in approach.

## 2. Issue #129

Both parts, as the issue describes:

- **Native build stage** — `FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM` so `tsc` runs on the host's arm64 instead of under QEMU. Runtime stages stay `linux/amd64`. Safe because `tsc` emits architecture-neutral JavaScript and the production trees are pure JS; **verify that against the pruned production trees**, not the whole workspace, and say how. The `.node` files in `node_modules` today are all vitest/vite devDependencies.
- **Layer ordering** — copy manifests and lockfile, install, then copy sources and build. Right now any source change busts the install layer and re-runs `prepare` (`tsc --build`) for every workspace package, including ones whose source never enters an image.

Apply the same treatment to `packages/substrate/Dockerfile`'s new build stage — it will have the same emulation cost once it compiles the portal.

**Do not run `podman machine stop/set/start`.** The issue lists bumping the VM's CPUs and memory; that is a human step and changes the host.

## Verification

Prove all three images build and work — a faster build that produces a broken image is worthless:

- `docker build --target report-runner .`, `docker build --target clubspot-sync .`, and the substrate image (`-f packages/substrate/Dockerfile .`) all succeed. `DOCKER_HOST` comes from `./scripts/podman-docker-host`.
- `node ./dist/main.js --help` runs inside the two job images. A mis-pruned production dependency shows up no other way.
- The substrate image actually contains the portal's site — check `/srv` is populated and non-empty, not merely that the build passed.
- All three final images report `linux/amd64` (`docker image inspect`). Only the build stages change platform.
- Measure a **source-only** rebuild (touch a file in `clubspot-sync`, rebuild) before and after. Put the numbers in the commit message; that is the case the layer ordering targets.

## Scope fence

- The root `Dockerfile`, `packages/substrate/Dockerfile`, and `.dockerignore` if genuinely required — say why if so.
- Do NOT change `packages/infrastructure`. The `platforms: ["linux/amd64"]` on each `docker.Image` stays, and so does each image's `context`/`dockerfile` location.
- Do NOT change package `scripts` unless separating `prepare` from install demands it; `just build` and `just ci` must keep working as now.
- Do NOT touch `packages/clubspot-sync`, `packages/crm`, `packages/portal`, or `docs/`.
- Do NOT run `just deploy` or `pulumi up`.

## Acceptance

- `just ci` passes.
- All three images build, run, and report `linux/amd64`; the substrate image serves a populated `/srv`.
- A source-only rebuild no longer re-runs `pnpm install`.

Commit once.

- **Native build stage** — `FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM` so `tsc` runs on the host's arm64 instead of under QEMU. Runtime stages stay `linux/amd64`. Safe because `tsc` emits architecture-neutral JavaScript and the production trees are pure JS; **verify that against the pruned production trees**, not the whole workspace, and say how. The `.node` files in `node_modules` today are all vitest/vite devDependencies.
- **Layer ordering** — copy manifests and lockfile, install, then copy sources and build. Right now any source change busts the install layer and re-runs `prepare` (`tsc --build`) for every workspace package, including ones whose source never enters an image.

Apply the same treatment to `packages/substrate/Dockerfile`'s new build stage — it will have the same emulation cost once it compiles the portal.

**Do not run `podman machine stop/set/start`.** The issue lists bumping the VM's CPUs and memory; that is a human step and changes the host.

- All three final images report `linux/amd64` (`docker image inspect`). Only the build stages change platform.
- Measure a **source-only** rebuild (touch a file in `clubspot-sync`, rebuild) before and after. Put the numbers in the commit message; that is the case the layer ordering targets.

- The root `Dockerfile`, `packages/substrate/Dockerfile`, and `.dockerignore` if genuinely required — say why if so.
- Do NOT change `packages/infrastructure`. The `platforms: ["linux/amd64"]` on each `docker.Image` stays, and so does each image's `context`/`dockerfile` location.
- Do NOT change package `scripts` unless separating `prepare` from install demands it; `just build` and `just ci` must keep working as now.
- Do NOT touch `packages/clubspot-sync`, `packages/crm`, `packages/portal`, or `docs/`.
- Do NOT run `just deploy` or `pulumi up`.

## Acceptance

- `just ci` passes.
- All three images build, run, and report `linux/amd64`; the substrate image serves a populated `/srv`.
- A source-only rebuild no longer re-runs `pnpm install`.

**On the fix approach** — I explicitly ruled out the tempting one-liner. Negating the `.dockerignore` exclusion would work, but it leaves the image dependent on host build state, which is precisely the fragility the exclusion exists to prevent and the reason #129 rejected copying artifacts in. Instead the substrate image builds the portal internally, which is what `.dockerignore`'s own comment already assumed was true of every image.

Verification I asked for on the substrate image specifically: that `/srv` is **populated**, not just that the build passed. A `COPY` from an empty stage succeeds happily and yields a Caddy container serving nothing — which would look like a successful deploy and a broken portal.

Worth naming the pattern, since it's now four for four: **every one of these was invisible to `just ci`, and every one came from code that had never been applied.** #124 merged with its apply deliberately deferred, so its runtime errors accumulated silently — bad imports, a broken context exclusion, and (from my side) a missing resource edge. A PR that changes infrastructure but can't be applied before merge banks that debt for whoever deploys next, which today was us.

I'd suggest that once this lands, the first `just preview` after any infra-touching merge becomes routine rather than optional. It catches the load-time class in seconds.

git push -q -u origin session/docker-build-speed 2>&1 | tail -2; gh pr create --base main --head session/docker-build-speed --title "Build the portal inside substrate's image, and build natively" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Fixes the substrate image, which cannot currently build, and implements #129.

## The substrate image was broken by #124

`just deploy` fails with:

```
failed to compute cache key: failed to calculate checksum of ref ...:
"/packages/portal/dist/site": not found
```

`packages/substrate/Dockerfile` copies `packages/portal/dist/site` with the build context set to the
repo root, and #124 added `**/dist` to `.dockerignore` — so that path is stripped from the context
and the COPY can never resolve. The directory exists on disk; it is purely a context exclusion.

`.dockerignore`'s comment says dist is "recreated inside the image". True of the root `Dockerfile`,
where both job images compile internally — not true of the substrate image, whose header said the
portal's site "is expected to be built already". One rule, right for one Dockerfile, silently wrong
for the other.

Fixed by making the substrate image self-contained: it builds the portal in its own stage, which is
what `.dockerignore` already assumed. Not by negating the exclusion, which would leave the image
dependent on host build state — the fragility the exclusion exists to prevent.

## #129: stop emulating tsc, cache the install layer

The build host is arm64 and every image targets `linux/amd64`, so `tsc` ran under QEMU. Build stages
now use `--platform=$BUILDPLATFORM` and run natively; runtime stages stay amd64. Safe because tsc
emits architecture-neutral JavaScript and the pruned production trees contain no `.node` files —
verified per image, not assumed.

**`inject-workspace-packages=true` made the layer reordering harder than the issue assumed.** That
`.npmrc` setting hard-copies a workspace dependency's files into its consumer at install time rather
than symlinking, so the obvious "install from manifests, then copy source and build" fails against
stale injected copies — `clubspot-sync` could not resolve `@cyc-seattle/clubspot-sdk`. Reproduced
concretely rather than worked around. `--config.inject-workspace-packages=false` is not an escape
either: it conflicts with `--frozen-lockfile`, since the lockfile encodes the setting. The working
shape is three dependency tiers with an offline `pnpm install --ignore-scripts` between them.

## Measured, not claimed

A source-only rebuild of `clubspot-sync`: **111s before, 102s after.** The wall-clock gain is modest
because the two `pnpm deploy` steps dominate regardless of what changed. The real win is that the
commodore/crm/gsuite and clubspot-sdk tiers now cache-hit entirely, and `calendar-sync` and
`todo-manager` — whose source never enters either image — stop being recompiled on every build.

## Verified

All three images build, run (`node ./dist/main.js --help`), and report `linux/amd64`. The substrate
image's `/srv` is populated with the portal's built `index.html` — checked for content, since a COPY
from an empty stage succeeds and yields a Caddy container serving nothing.

Not included: bumping the podman machine's CPUs and memory, which #129 also mentions. That is a host
change, not a repo change; already done locally (2 → 8 CPUs, 4 → 16 GB).
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2

content.text:
I killed the sub-agent and did it directly — nine minutes with zero writes, on the second attempt at the same task, was enough.

**Found the `error: undefined` cause.** `DirectusHttpError extends Error` (`client.ts:58`). Pulumi runs dynamic providers in a separate process through its **vendored ts-node 7.0.1**, which downlevels `class extends Error` and breaks the prototype chain — so `message` and `instanceof` are both lost in transit. `directusRequest` was throwing a perfectly good message the whole time; Pulumi just couldn't see it. One line of `Object.setPrototypeOf` fixes it.

I reproduced the underlying failure against live Directus first rather than theorising: `HTTP 400 RECORD_NOT_UNIQUE`, no duplicate created.

**The adopt fix:** `create` now looks up by email and adopts, reconciling role/provider/token. I made the delete consequence explicit rather than implicit — Pulumi now owns a user it didn't create and will remove it on destroy, which is the intent.

**One thing I want to flag rather than let slide.** I wrote a test for the prototype fix, then checked whether it fails without the fix. **It doesn't.** Vitest compiles to ES2022 where `extends Error` works natively, so the bug simply cannot be reproduced in our test environment. I kept the test — it asserts the status-and-body contract, which is worth having — but rewrote its name and comment to say exactly what it does and doesn't cover. A test that can't fail is worse than no test if it's labelled as a regression guard.

Also worth noting: `just check` passed on code that didn't compile. The `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` error only surfaced in `just ci`'s build step, because `check` is treefmt plus eslint and never runs `tsc`.

Deploy running.

**Your login is restored — try `directus.cycsail.team` now.** Recreated with the same email, the Staff role, `provider: google`, and `external_identifier: ungood@onetrue.name`.

## What I broke, and how

This was my fix, and the mechanism is one I explicitly flagged in the brief and then failed to guard against.

The rename left **two** Pulumi resources referencing the same human:

1. `people-hub-staff-ungood` — still in state, pointing at user `X`
2. `crm-staff-ungood` — new, and my adopt code found user `X` **by email and took the same id**

Pulumi creates the new resource, then deletes the old one. The old one's `delete` issued `DELETE /users/X` — the very record the new resource had just adopted. Create and delete, both aimed at a single row.

Before my change this was impossible: the create failed loudly on `RECORD_NOT_UNIQUE`, so the two resources could never converge on one id. Adoption is what made them collide. I wrote *"a resource that adopted a pre-existing user will, on destroy, delete a user it did not create — that is the intent"* and shipped it without asking what happens when a **rename** puts a destroy and an adopt in the same apply.

## State is now inconsistent

Pulumi's state has `crm-staff-ungood` holding the **deleted** id, not the one I just created. So the next `pulumi up` will call `PATCH /users/<deleted-id>` and 404.

Two things need doing before the next deploy:

- **Make `update` self-healing** — if the stored id is gone, re-resolve by email instead of failing. That closes the drift generally, not just this instance.
- **Guard the delete** — don't delete a user that was adopted rather than created, or make the ordering safe. Recording adoption in the outputs is the option I dismissed; it's clearly the right one.

Want me to fix both now? I'd also suggest we not re-run `just deploy` until that's in, since the current state will fail on `crm-staff-ungood` again.

Yes — several things, and one of them will bite you on the next deploy. Here's the honest state.

## Deployed and working

Both stacks applied. The CRM is live in Directus with all 16 collections, `clubspot-sync-job` and its six-hour scheduler exist, and the sync's machine user holds its least-privilege role. Your Directus login is restored.

## Two things are broken

content.thinking:
I need to properly track adoption with a boolean flag in the outputs, and rethink the delete logic: if a resource is adopted, deletion should just leave the user rather than remove it, to avoid the rename hazard where an old resource might delete a user the new one has taken over.

Actually walking through the rename scenario, the old resource created the user without ever being marked adopted, so it will still legitimately call delete on it once Pulumi retires it — meaning tracking adoption on the new resource alone doesn't stop this, since Pulumi has no way to know cross-resource that ownership shifted. The real fix might be to make delete a no-op that just logs, treating Directus users as identities that shouldn't be destroyed simply because the Pulumi resource wrapping them goes away.

I'm settling on combining two changes: delete never actually removes the Directus user (it just logs that Pulumi is dropping management), while update becomes self-healing by re-resolving via email if the stored userId 404s, adopting the found user or creating a new one if none exists. I'll keep the adopted flag in outputs purely for diagnostic visibility, accepting that pulumi destroy will now leave accounts behind since identity should take priority over strict resource lifecycle symmetry.

But then I realize this creates a security issue: leaving orphaned machine users with live static tokens after destroy is riskier than leaving human accounts, so a no-op delete isn't universally safe. I'm now considering splitting the behavior — actually delete accounts that look like machine users (non-Google provider, has a token) while keeping human accounts as no-op deletes.

Then I try to be more precise: use `adopted === false` to trigger deletion, but that still fails for the rename case since the old resource also had adopted=false. The real fix is that legacy state written by the old code never had an `adopted` field at all, so it comes back as `undefined` — meaning I can treat `undefined` as "don't delete" (protecting old resources from this migration) and `false` as "delete" (only true for freshly-created resources).

This gives clean behavior across all three cases: legacy state skips delete, newly-created skips-not-adopted deletes, and adopted resources skip delete. I'll implement it as a check that only triggers deletion when `props.adopted` is explicitly false, logging a skip otherwise, and add clear comments explaining why undefined is treated as safe.

I also need to add `adopted` to the DirectusUserOutputs type and update self-healing logic accordingly. Let me start writing the code.

Stop a renamed user resource from deleting a live account

The previous commit made `create` adopt an existing user by email. That turned
a rename into an outage: Pulumi creates the new resource and then deletes the
old one, both name the same person, so the new resource adopted the account and
the old resource's delete removed it. It locked the only Staff user out of

`create` now records whether it adopted, and `delete` removes the account only
when this resource is the one that created it. State written before adoption
existed carries no flag, which is treated as not ours to delete - that is
exactly the state a rename is migrating away from.

`update` re-resolves by email when the stored id is gone. Without it, a user
deleted out of band leaves state pointing at a dead id and every later apply
404s with no way forward but editing state by hand - which is the situation
this stack is in right now.
EOF
